requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The specification occupies one page and explains a photographic concept spanning shore, microhabitat and organism scales. It includes eight distinct shot records: W1 and W2 at shore scale, M1 and M2 at microhabitat scale, and O1, O2, D1 and D2 at organism scale, with the D shots identified as shell details. W1 establishes the study area, W2 locates both samples, M1/O1/D1 concern L1 at S1, and M2/O2/D2 concern P1 at S2. Proposed viewpoints are stated and may vary creatively. The lighting plan uses diffuse ambient daylight, with initial settings f/8 and 1/250 s, and records the session and low-water facts. Missing records, wrong assignments or contradictory starting settings fail.

Each target explicitly restates the specification's session window, BST time zone, low-water time and height, and ambient diffuse lighting approach. Compare photograph entries against the specification for unchanged shot identifiers and sample assignments. Rephrasing and different placement are acceptable; omission, reassignment or disagreement fails, including a shared value that contradicts the client's fixed record.

W1 establishes the study shore and W2 makes S1 and S2 locatable within that same setting. Assess spatial relationships against the supplied site plan and records: a 20000 mm east–west by 12000 mm north–south area, southwest origin, eastward x and northward y, north landward and south seaward. S1 is at (6000, 4000) on exposed rock; S2 is at (14000, 6000) on the margin of the pool bounded by x 12000–16000 and y 6000–9000. M1 shows damp grey rock with L1 above standing water; M2 shows grey rock with P1 beside the pool waterline. Perspective and camera direction may vary, and coordinates need not be overprinted, but sample swaps, incompatible geography or incompatible water context fail.

The L1 views depict the same grey-white conical limpet shell with radiating ribs and an apex slightly forward of centre; the P1 views depict the same dark grey-brown pointed periwinkle shell with six whorls, a lighter apex and dark spiral lines. Compare with the respective supplied identity references. Whole-organism views show the complete shells, D1 resolves the radiating ribs, and D2 resolves the spiral surface. Recorded measurements remain 32 mm shell length for L1 and 18 mm shell height for P1. Viewpoint and magnification may change, and detail crops need not show the entire organism; changed identity, incompatible visible morphology or sample reassignment fails.

The subject series visibly preserves each shell's placement relative to its surrounding substrate and water, with soft illumination consistent with ambient coastal daylight. Changes in framing, camera position and exposure are acceptable. Visible relocation, studio staging or lighting incompatible with diffuse daylight fails. Do not infer numerical camera settings from image appearance; those are assessed in the written records.

Each whole-organism image has a legible bar representing 5 mm, and each detail image has a legible bar representing 1 mm, with the required label. Delivered image or record evidence must support calibration using the supplied ruler in the relevant subject plane. The ruler has a 50 mm measuring span, 1 mm graduations and numbering at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50; its body is 60 by 15 mm, matte white with black markings. Distinguish measuring span from body length. Bar styling may vary, but wrong represented lengths, unsupported calibration or calibration from an incompatible plane fails. Account for perspective rather than demanding a naive shell-to-bar ratio.

The document explicitly identifies L1's 32 mm measurement as shell length and P1's 18 mm measurement as shell height. Wording may vary while retaining those meanings. Reversed axes, incorrect values or measurements presented without the required distinction fail.

One output is square and the other is portrait. Both are recognizable crops of O1, preserving the complete original shell, its caption and a labelled 5 mm bar. The bar's displayed length must remain calibrated to the shell after each crop's resizing; an unchanged pixel length is acceptable only if image magnification is unchanged. Different framing is allowed. Substituted shell imagery, clipped shell parts, missing captions or bars, and incorrect recalibration fail.

Across all ten layouts, the caption occupies the bottom 15% of frame height and the image inset follows 5% of frame width and height, consistent with the supplied crop-geometry reference. O1, O2 and both O1 crops keep every part of the whole shell inside that inset. Assess proportional geometry at the available viewing resolution without requiring particular pixel dimensions. Different proportions and compositions are permitted; missing zones, materially incorrect margins or shells extending outside the required inset fail.

Eight numbered photographs appear in this order: W1, W2, M1, O1, D1, M2, O2, D2. Their captions preserve the correct specimen/sample pairings and scientific names. Observations agree with the referenced photographs, addressing shell appearance where visible and the substrate and water conditions available in each view. Every capture time falls within 08:30–09:50 BST. Natural variation in descriptive language is acceptable; sequence errors, missing photographs, misidentification, out-of-window times or observations contradicted by the images fail.

Photograph entries include shot identifiers, capture times, tide context and recorded camera settings, with specimen/sample identifiers, common names, scientific names and measurements associated with the relevant subjects. L1/S1 is Common limpet, Patella vulgata, shell length 32 mm; P1/S2 is Common periwinkle, Littorina littorea, shell height 18 mm. Shore entries may cover both samples or identify an establishing view without inventing a single specimen assignment. The record identifies 18 September 2026 and uses BST. Tide statements agree with 1.1 m and falling at 08:30, 0.8 m and low water at 09:10, and 1.0 m and rising at 09:50, all above chart datum; do not require invented intermediate heights. Actual camera settings may differ from the initial settings if recorded accurately. Missing required fields or contradictory records fail.

Each photographic layout has a readable caption connecting observations to the applicable supplied records. Shell descriptions must fit what the view reveals, and substrate and water descriptions must fit the visible scene; shore or tight-detail views need not claim features outside their frame. Subject captions preserve L1/S1 and P1/S2 and distinguish 32 mm shell length from 18 mm shell height where measurements are given; the O and D captions explicitly retain that measurement distinction. Crops preserve O1's caption information. Missing captions, incorrect subject records or invented visible conditions fail.

The written feature consistently situates the work at West Ledge during the specified date and BST session. The specification records the study extent and session date, and all three documents include the required session window and low-water record of 09:10 BST at 0.8 m above chart datum. References to site dimensions, date, orientation or tide elsewhere must agree with the supplied records. Different units expressing the same physical extent are acceptable; changed dates, time zones, extents or tide datum fail.

Review the full video and its duration. It runs for 10 seconds and progresses through recognizable W1, M1, O1, M2 and O2 imagery in that order. The opening visibly prints LEDGE TO LIFE and A shore at three scales, and the video legibly presents the low-water time as 09:10 BST. Transitions and allocation of time among shots are discretionary. Wrong duration, missing or reordered views, incorrect imagery, absent opening text or an incorrect low-water time fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation contains at least eight pages, with the exact feature title and opening line on page one. Page labels, headings or a contents guide clearly identify where the specification facts, caption sequence and video storyboard appear. The storyboard represents W1, M1, O1, M2 and O2 in the video order. Pagination and grouping may vary. Too few pages, misplaced or missing opening wording, absent required sections or an incompatible storyboard fails.

Verify identifiable reuse of every listed source: the specification's content, all eight distinct photographs, both distinct O1 crop layouts and the caption sequence. Documents may be integrated through readable excerpts or faithful reformatting, and images may be resized for the presentation while remaining recognizable. A source name without its content, a substitute image, an omitted crop or omitted photograph fails. The included video storyboard must visibly relate to the commissioned observation sequence.

The photographs form a coherent progression from the same West Ledge shore through its two microhabitats to whole shells and shell details, preserving subject positions, sample assignments and recognizable surroundings. The photographic evidence and captions agree with the specification and sequence records for shot identity, subject identity and diffuse ambient daylight.

Every photographic layout follows the required bottom 15% caption zone and 5% outer inset, with complete whole shells contained inside the inset in O1, O2 and both O1 crops. O1 and its two crops preserve the same photographic shell and caption information while their displayed 5 mm scale bars remain calibrated to each rendering. Whole-organism views use labelled 5 mm bars and detail views use labelled 1 mm bars, with records consistently distinguishing limpet shell length from periwinkle shell height.
